rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic إن marks the statement as important and indirectly expresses that God approves the Prophet’s night vigil, preparing for the later easing as mercy and honor.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية عن أنه أرضى ربه بذلك وتوطئة للتخفيف الذي سيذكر في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Hijra, the Prophet’s duties in governing, defending Medina, and preparing armies left less daytime leisure than in Mecca, explaining the easing of obligatory and recommended night prayer.
rows.anchor: ما كان له فيه أيام مقامه بمكة ، فظهرت حكمة الله في التخفيف عن رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet divided his home time among God, family, and himself, then devoted his own share to people, meeting their needs and guiding them.
rows.anchor: حديث علي بن أبي طالب ( أنه سئل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أوى إلى منزله فقال : كان إذا أوى إلى منزله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect يعلم suggests continuing, renewed knowledge and thereby signals that the Prophet’s conduct is pleasing to God.
rows.anchor: وإيثار المضارع في قوله : { يعلم } للدلالة على استمرار ذلك العلم وتجدده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, يعلم in 33:18 occurs in a reproach: God has continually known the obstructors’ conduct, and no part of it is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: وفي ضده قوله : { قد يعلم الله المعوقين منكم } ( الأحزاب : 18 ) لأنه في معرض التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أدنى literally means nearer, from دنو; it is metaphorically used for less because the distance to the nearest thing is small, just as farther can denote more.
rows.anchor: و { أدنى } أصله أقرب ، من الدنو ، استعير للأقل لأن المسافة التي بين الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أدنى is an adverbial accusative with تقوم: the Prophet stands for a period shorter than two thirds, meaning more than half, as 73:4 indicates.
rows.anchor: وهو منصوب على الظرفية لفعل { تقوم } ، أي تقوم في زمان يقدر أقل من ثلثي الليل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ثلثي with a vowelled lām, its original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { ثلثي } بضم اللام على الأصل

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers put ونصفه وثلثه in the genitive, coordinating them with ثلثي الليل: the vigil is for less than half or less than a third.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب { ونصفه وثلثه } بخفضهما عطفا على

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: These readers put ونصفه وثلثه in the accusative as objects of تقوم, describing standing for two thirds, half, or a third, without going below half or a third.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف بنصب { ونصفه وثلثه } على أنهما منصوبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings describe different nightly patterns as nights and days vary in length; all fit the choice granted in 73:2–4, so the intended meaning does not change.
rows.anchor: وهذه أحوال مختلفة في قيام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالليل تابعة لاختلاف أحوال الليالي والأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical statement that God measures night and day fits here because He knows all the possible durations and has made them known; readings therefore do not alter the point.
rows.anchor: وبه تظهر مناسبة تعقيب هذه الجملة بالجملة المعترضة ، وهي جملة { والله يقدر الليل والنهار }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects al-Farrāʾ’s assertion that the accusative reading is closer to correct, since the readings preserve the same intended meaning.
rows.anchor: فمن العجاب قول الفراء أن النصب أشبه بالصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طائفة is nominative, coordinated with إن’s noun after its predicate; this is permitted by treating it as a new clause, as in 9:3.
rows.anchor: و { طائفة } عطف على اسم { إن } بالرفع وهو وجه جائز إذا كان بعد ذكر خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction subtly marks the different status and measure of the Prophet’s vigil and the group’s; 9:3 likewise distinguishes God’s disavowal from the Messenger’s public dealings with polytheists.
rows.anchor: فإن بين قيام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيام الطائفة التي معه تفاوتا في الحكم والمقدار

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports in Sahih al-Bukhari that people joined the Prophet’s mosque prayer on successive Ramadan nights, growing in number; he stayed away later for fear the prayer would be made obligatory.
rows.anchor: ففي حديث عائشة في ( صحيح البخاري ) ( أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى ذات ليلة في المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If معك means figurative association, fellowship, and agreement rather than physical attendance at night prayer, the group includes several Companions and Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, whose night-prayer reports occur separately in Sahih al-Bukhari.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت المعية معية مجازية وهي الانتساب والصحبة والموافقة فقد عددنا منهم : عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s opening praises the Prophet for faithfully fulfilling the night vigil and praises the group who followed him.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن صدر هذه الآية إيماء إلى الثناء على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في وفائه بقيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge that the Prophet stands is an indirect expression of divine approval of their practice.
rows.anchor: فالخبر بأن الله يعلم أنك تقوم مراد به الكناية عن الرضى عنهم فيما فعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening statement prepares for the ensuing explanation that they cannot keep the vigil’s full measure.
rows.anchor: والمقصود : التمهيد لقوله : { علم أن لن تحصوه } إلى آخر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb علم is repeated rather than coordinated with وأن سيكون to mark this as a distinct consideration in the easing.
rows.anchor: أعيد فعل { علم } في جملة { علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: والله يقدر الليل والنهار is a parenthesis between God’s knowledge of the vigil and the statement that they cannot fully measure it; its relevance was explained above.
rows.anchor: وجملة { والله يقدر الليل والنهار } معترضة بين جملتي { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be a second predicate of إن after the vigil clause, or an explanatory resumption answering the listener’s expectation; after commending them, God eases their burden.
rows.anchor: أن تكون خبرا ثانيا عن { إن } بعد الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object pronoun in تحصوه refers to the night standing understood from أنك تقوم.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى القيام المستفاد من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إحصاء literally means counting, from حصى because pebbles were used to count; here it metaphorically means being able to sustain the many acts of bowing, prostration, and recitation.
rows.anchor: والإحصاء حقيقته : معرفة عدد شيء معدود مشتق من اسم الحصى جمع حصاة

rows.speaker: الحسن وسفيان
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Sufyan explain إحصاء here as ability to manage the many actions of night prayer.
rows.anchor: وبهذا فسر الحسن وسفيان ، ومنه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited hadith says to be steadfast, since full steadfastness cannot be attained; take on as much as one can bear.
rows.anchor: في الحديث استقيموا ولن تحصوا أي ولن تطيقوا تمام الاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is the lightened form of الثقيلة, with an omitted pronoun of شأن and a sentential predicate; the negative particle separates it from its verbal predicate in standard usage.
rows.anchor: أن } مخففة من الثقيلة ، واسمها ضمير شأن محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن and its clause fill both object positions of علم; the sense is that He knew their inability to keep count would in fact occur.
rows.anchor: وجملتها سادة مسد مفعولي { علم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تاب is metaphorical for withholding blame before a lapse occurs: anticipated shortfall resembles an actual sin, so language of repentance describes the lifting of liability.
rows.anchor: وفعل { تاب } مستعار لعدم المؤاخذة قبل حصول التقصير لأن التقصير متوقع فشابه الحاصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address from تحصوه onward targets Muslims who kept night vigil, either by a shift from third to second person or by a general expression narrowed by context; the Prophet himself could count, while illness and other duties are mentioned.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن يكون الخطاب في قوله : { تحصوه } وما بعده موجها إلى المسلمين الذين كانوا يقومون الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاقرؤوا ما تيسر من القرآن means perform as much prayer as is manageable, since prayer necessarily includes recitation.
rows.anchor: فصلوا ما تيسر لكم ، ولما كانت الصلاة لا تخلو عن قراءة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling prayer Qurʾān, as in 17:78’s قرآن الفجر for the dawn prayer, concisely encourages both night worship and recitation.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { وقرآن الفجر } ( الإسراء : 78 ) أي صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran meant here is what had been revealed before this Medinan verse: all the Meccan Quran and some Medinan revelation; it differs from the earlier command to recite with measured cadence.
rows.anchor: والمراد القرآن الذي كان نزل قبل هذه الآية المدنية وهو شيء كثير من القرآن المكي كله وشيء من المدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase concerns as much night prayer as manageable, not the minimum Quranic recitation required in prayer; even if read as recitation, the amount is unspecified here and clarified by the hadith requiring al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: فلا دلالة في هذه الآية على مقدار ما يجزىء من القراءة في الصلاة إذ ليس سياقها في هذا المهيع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The cited Prophetic hadith states that prayer is not valid for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.
rows.anchor: وقد بينه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب )

rows.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء
rows.claim: The majority of jurists require a surah in addition to al-Fātiḥa and consider reciting only part of a surah in obligatory prayer disliked; partial recitation is allowed in night prayer, Ramadan vigil, and necessity.
rows.anchor: وهو الواجب عند جمهور الفقهاء ، فيكره أن يقرأ المصلي بعض سورة في الفريضة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in the Ṣaḥīḥ says the Prophet became hoarse while reciting and bowed in the middle of a surah, illustrating an exception for night prayer or need.
rows.anchor: ففي ( الصحيح ) ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ فأخذته بحة فركع )

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأحمد في رواية
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and one report from Ahmad hold that even a short single verse suffices and al-Fātiḥa is not specifically required; they cite 55:64 as an example, while Abu Hanifa’s two companions disagree on both points.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأحمد في رواية عنه : تجزىء قراءة آية من القرآن ولو كانت قصيرة

rows.speaker: صاحبا أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa’s two companions disagree with him on both whether one short verse suffices and whether al-Fātiḥa is required.
rows.anchor: وخالفه صاحباه في الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed rules specifying when an imam, follower, or person praying alone must recite are treated in legal manuals.
rows.anchor: وتعيين من تجب عليه القراءة من منفرد وإمام ومأموم مبين في كتب الفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When تاب means accepting repentance, it takes على by implication of مِن; when it means turning away from and regretting sin, it takes a preposition suited to that sense.
rows.anchor: إذا أريد به قبول توبة التائب عدي بحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse abrogates the set duration of night vigil—half the night or more or less than a third—leaving its amount unmeasured; the vigil’s remaining legal status was explained earlier.
rows.anchor: وقد نسخت هذه الآية تحديد مدة قيام الليل بنصفه أو أزيد أو أقل من ثلثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about illness and other circumstances is an elaboration of the inability to keep the measure, and gives another easing for additional conditions.
rows.anchor: هذه الجملة بدل اشتمال من جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first broad category of reasons for easing is impaired health, represented by the mention of the sick.
rows.anchor: أعذار اختلال الصحة وقد شملها قوله

words: وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second category is livelihood work—trade, crafts, farming, and similar necessities—summarized as traveling in search of God’s provision.
rows.anchor: الأشغال التي تدعو إليها ضرورة العيش من تجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third category is work for the community: fighting, frontier watch and garrison duty, army management, and sending envoys or ambassadors to spread Islam; it includes the Prophet’s fighting and illness.
rows.anchor: الضرب الثالث : أعمال لمصالح الأمة وأشار إليها قوله : { وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith reports that the Prophet fell ill and missed the night vigil for one or two nights.
rows.anchor: اشتكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If this verse was revealed in Mecca, it foretells the Muslims’ coming independence and ability against their enemies; if Medinan, it excuses the raids and campaigns they had begun.
rows.anchor: وإذا كانت هذه الآية مما نزل بمكة ففيها بشارة بأن أمر المسلمين صائر إلى استقلال وقترة على أعدائهم

words: وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Companions infer the virtue of trade and travel from God’s placing lawful earners alongside fighters; these two reasons honor such activities, while other excused needs resemble illness.
rows.anchor: وقد كان بعض الصحابة يتأول من هذه الآية فضيلة التجارة والسفر للتجر حيث سوى الله بين المجاهدين والمكتسبين المال الحلال

words: وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says that one who brings goods to a Muslim city seeking God’s approval and sells them at the day’s price has a standing with God like the martyrs; he cites this verse.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن مسعود أنه قال ( أيما رجل جلب شيئا إلى مدينة من مدائن المسلمين

words: وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that after death in God’s path, he would prefer to die between his travel packs while journeying in search of God’s bounty.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر : ( ما خلق الله موتة بعد الموت في سبيل الله أحب إلي من أن أموت بين شعبتي رحلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يضربون في الأرض means traveling across the earth.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { يضربون في الأرض } يسيرون في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root image is one body striking another; travel is called striking the earth because يضربون incorporates walking, while the striking sense fades and في marks earth as the place traversed.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الضرب : قرع جسم بجسم آخر ، وسمي السير في الأرض ضربا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s bounty means seeking provision; 2:198 uses the expression for trade during the Hajj period.
rows.anchor: والابتغاء من فضل الله طلب الرزق قال تعالى

words: يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here traveling for God’s bounty means business travel: journeys often occupy both night and day, requiring travelers to sleep by day.
rows.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله } مراد بالضرب في الأرض فيه السفر للتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in منه refers to the Quran.
rows.anchor: وفرع عليه مثل ما فرع على الذي قبله فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The measure of night prayer is entrusted to what is manageable for all Muslims despite their differing excuses.
rows.anchor: وقد نيط مقدار القيام بالتيسير على جميع المسلمين وإن اختلفت الأعذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse either lifts night prayer’s obligation if it had previously been obligatory, or clarifies that it was never obligatory and that Muslims’ voluntary imitation of the Prophet was not binding.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية اقتضت رفع وجوب قيام الليل عن المسلمين إن كان قد وجب عليهم من قبل على أحد الاحتمالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer was not made obligatory, or its obligation was lifted, because widespread excuses make it burdensome; a general presumption of hardship can remove obligation where individuals otherwise might receive only temporary exemptions.
rows.anchor: وعلل عدم وجوبه عليهم بأن الأمة يكثر فيها أصحاب الأعذار التي يشق معها قيام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a rule based on the general likelihood of hardship: like travel prayer remaining two rakʿahs because travel usually brings hardship, according to ʿĀʾisha’s report.
rows.anchor: فتبين أن هذا تعليل الحكم الشرعي بالمظنة والحكم هنا عدمي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that prayer was first prescribed as two rakʿahs, then three prayers were lengthened at home while travel prayer remained two.
rows.anchor: على قول عائشة أم المؤمنين : ( إن الصلاة فرضت ركعتين ثم زيد في ثلاث من الصلوات في الحضر وأبقيت صلاة السفر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concession was warranted because night prayer is not one of Islam’s pillars, so its religious benefit was not weighty enough to require it universally.
rows.anchor: وأوجب الترخص في قيام الليل أنه لم يكن ركنا من أركان الإسلام فلم تكن المصلحة الدينية قوية فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer remains governed by the earlier command in 73:2 and the Sunnah’s encouragement of it; Ibn ʿĀshūr says he explained this already.
rows.anchor: وأما حكم القيام فهو ما دل عليه قوله : { قم الليل إلا قليلا } ( المزمل : 2 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse grounds legal reasoning from a broadly likely condition and supports general concessions for hardship common to most people, such as advance-payment sale, rather than isolated personal cases.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية صالحة لأن تكون أصلا للتعليل بالمظنة وصالحة لأن تكون أصلا تقاس عليه الرخص العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish prayer reminds believers to guard the obligatory prayers and not neglect them, as stated in 4:103.
rows.anchor: تذكير بأن الصلوات الواجبة هي التي تحرصون على إقامتها وعدم التفريط فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The juxtaposition suggests that the five obligatory prayers discharge believers’ duty, while night prayer is voluntary and greatly beneficial; many transmitted reports support this.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أن في الصلوات الخمس ما يرفع التبعة عن المؤمنين وأن قيام الليل نافلة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakah are commonly paired in revelation; Abu Bakr inferred that zakah refusal warrants fighting, telling ʿUmar he would fight anyone who separated them.
rows.anchor: حتى استنبط أبو بكر رضي الله عنه من ذلك أن مانع الزكاة يقاتل عليها

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr told ʿUmar that he would fight anyone who distinguished between prayer and zakah.
rows.anchor: فقال لعمر رضي الله عنه ( لأقاتلن من فرق بين الصلاة والزكاة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lending to God means voluntary charity; giving to the poor is likened to a loan because God promises a generous return in the reward of the Last Day.
rows.anchor: وإقراض الله هو الصدقات غير الواجبة ، شبه إعطاء الصدقة للفقير بقرض يقرضه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A good loan is charity given solely for God’s sake and free of reminders or injury; goodness varies by degree and by the qualities valued in each kind of charity.
rows.anchor: ووصف القرض بالحسن يفيد الصدقة المراد بها وجه الله تعالى والسالمة من المن والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr links this expression to the earlier parallels in 2:245 and 64:17, where lending God a good loan is promised multiplied reward.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في سورة البقرة قوله : { من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه له ضعافا كثيرة وفي سورة التغابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This closing statement summarizes prior commands and gives an omitted command: do good; whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find with God.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام إيجاز حذف . تقدير المحذوف : وافعلوا الخير وما تقدموا لأنفسكم منه تجدوه عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw may coordinate this command with the preceding statement, making it a concluding exhortation to repair lapses in commanded good, including repentance for neglected obligations.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الواو للعطف فيكون معطوفا على جملة { وما تقدموا لأنفسكم } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is conditional.
rows.anchor: و { ما } شرطية . ومعنى تقديم الخير : فعله في الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good in worldly life for its afterlife reward is pictured as a traveler sending ahead luggage, tools, and family to the destination so they are ready on arrival.
rows.anchor: شبه فعل الخير في مدة الحياة لرجاء الانتفاع بثوابه في الحياة الآخرة بتقديم العازم على السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من خير explains the otherwise indefinite ما.
rows.anchor: و { من خير } بيان لإبهام { ما } الشرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good is what religion identifies as praiseworthy and promises to reward.
rows.anchor: والخير : هو ما وصفه الدين بالحسن ووعد على فعله بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تجدوه means finding the deed’s reward and recompense; scripture often names compensation by the thing for which it is given.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { تجدوه } تجدوا جزاءه وثوابه ، وهو الذي قصده فاعله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith says a person who hoards wealth without paying its due will meet a bald snake on Judgment Day saying, I am your wealth, your treasure.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الذي يكنز المال ولا يؤدي حقه ( مثل له يوم القيامة شجاعا أقرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in تجدوه is the first object of تجدوا and خيرا is its second object.
rows.anchor: وضمير الغائب في { تجدوه } هو المفعول الأول ل ( تجدوا ) ومفعوله الثاني { خيرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intervening pronoun is a separating pronoun even before an indefinite; this is allowed because أفعل من كذا resembles a definite noun, which cannot take the definite article.
rows.anchor: والضمير المنفصل الذي بينهما ضمير فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خير is a comparative: the reward found is better than what was sent ahead, meaning the deed’s recompense is multiplied, as 64:17 promises.
rows.anchor: و { خيرا } : اسم تفضيل ، أي خيرا مما تقدمونه إذ ليس المراد أنكم تجدونه من جنس الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun here intensifies certainty.
rows.anchor: وأفاد ضمير الفصل هنا مجرد التأكيد لتحقيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأعظم أجرا either coordinates with خيرا, extending the separating pronoun’s emphasis, or independently carries that emphasis; أجرا is an accusative specification of أعظم.
rows.anchor: وعطف { وأعظم أجرا } على { خيرا } أو هو منسحب عليه تأكيد ضمير الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw begins an explanatory resumption: after easing night prayer, God directs believers to seek forgiveness in the night’s late hours as another devotional practice.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الواو للاستئناف وتكون الجملة استئنافا بيانيا ناشئا عن الترخيص في ترك بعض القيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Late-night forgiveness seeking accords with 51:18 and with two Prophetic reports about the last third of the night and waking from sleep.
rows.anchor: وهو مشمول لقوله تعالى : { وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون } ( الذاريات : 18 )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that each night, in its final third, God calls for people to pray, ask, or seek forgiveness, promising response, giving, and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ينزل ربنا كل ليلة إلى سماء الدنيا حين يبقى ثلث الليل الآخر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that one who wakes at night, recites the stated remembrance, and then asks forgiveness or supplicates will have the request answered.
rows.anchor: وقال : ( من تعار من الليل فقال : لا إلاه إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s great forgiveness and mercy explain the command to seek forgiveness and encourage it as likely to be answered; the intensive descriptions hint at that promise.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن الله غفور رحيم } تعليل للأمر بالاستغفار ، أي لأن الله كثير المغفرة شديد الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف in فأنذر marks the immediate transition from alerting and beginning to the command to warn.
rows.anchor: وأفادت فاء { فأنذر } تعقيب إفادة التحفز والشروع بالأمر بإيقاع الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قم is treated as intransitive; the consequent فأنذر clarifies what rising is meant to accomplish.
rows.anchor: منزلة اللازم ، وتفريع { فأنذر } عليه يبين المراد من الأمر بالقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the Prophet as wrapped in fear at seeing the angel of revelation, Ibn ʿĀshūr reads the command as reassurance: do not fear and undertake warning.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : يا أيها المدثر من الرعب لرؤية ملك الوحي لا تخف وأقبل على الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This appears to be the first revealed command to preach: al-ʿAlaq contains no call to invite, while 73:15 and 73:11 presuppose that the Prophet had already preached and faced deniers.
rows.anchor: والظاهر : أن هذه الآية أول ما نزل في الأمر بالدعوة لأن سورة العلق لم تتضمن أمرا بالدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning comes first because it gathers caution against improper conduct and its consequences; removing harms precedes adorning with virtues, and people then chiefly needed warning.
rows.anchor: التخلية مقدمة على التحلية ودرء المفاسد مقدم على جلب المصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of أنذر is omitted to convey generality: warn all people, except Khadija, who had believed and thus merited glad tidings.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { أنذر } محذوف لإفادة العموم ، أي أنذر الناس كلهم وهم يومئذ جميع الناس ما عدا خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربك is the object of كبر, fronted before its verb to express restriction: magnify no one else, particularly the idols; this is restriction of individuals.
rows.anchor: انتصب { ربك } على المفعولية لفعل ( كبر ) قذم على عامله لإفادة الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw connects the command to magnify the Lord with the preceding command to rise and warn in 74:2.
rows.anchor: والواو عطفت جملة { ربك فكبر } على جملة { قم فأنذر } ( المدثر : 2 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف may signal a general omitted condition, with كبر as its answer; fronting the object prepares this construction, so the sense is magnify God in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: ودخلت الفاء على ( كبر ) إيذانا بشرط محذوف يكون ( كبر ) جوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an example of a fronted complement functioning like a condition, Ibn ʿĀshūr cites the Prophetic instruction ففيهما فجاهد about one’s parents.
rows.anchor: لأن تقديم المعمول قد ينزل منزلة الشرط كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ففيهما فجاهد )

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni allows that the ف could be extra, as in زيدا فاضرب meaning simply strike Zayd.
rows.anchor: وجوز ابن جني أن تكون الفاء زائدة قال : هو كقولك زيدا فاضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تكبير means magnifying; the form attributes the root quality to its object, metaphorically likening what is honored to something great in its class because of its superior qualities.
rows.anchor: وتكبير الرب تعظيمه ففعل ( كبر ) يفيد معنى نسبة مفعوله إلى أصل مادة اشتقاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to describe the Lord with attributes of greatness: transcendence from defects, exclusive divinity, denial of offspring, and all attributes of perfection.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { وربك فكبر : } صف ربك بصفات التعظيم ، وهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnifying God includes inward conviction and verbal glorification and instruction.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( كبر ) : كبره في اعتقادك : وكبره بقولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command includes saying الله أكبر, which declares God greater and more exalted than every great thing; this is why the phrase opens prayer.
rows.anchor: ويشمل هذا المعنى أن يقول : ( الله أكبر ) لأنه إذا قال هذه الكلمة أفاد وصف الله بأنه أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of magnification may signal the institution of prayer, especially beside the command to purify clothes; a report in Muslim says this preceded the prescription of prayer, which Ibn ʿĀshūr takes to mean prayer was prescribed after this surah, not the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: في ذكر التكبير إيماء إلى شرع الصلاة التي أولها التكبير وخاصة اقترانه بقوله : { وثيابك فطهر }

rows.speaker: معمر عن الزهري
rows.claim: A report from Maʿmar via al-Zuhrī in Muslim says this occurred before prayer was prescribed; Ibn ʿĀshūr infers an early prayer distinct from the five daily prayers, since the Prophet did pray in the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: ووقع في رواية معمر عن الزهري عند مسلم أن قال : وذلك قبل أن تفرض الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form of the garment-purification command parallels 74:3: do not leave your clothes unpurified.
rows.anchor: هو في النظم مثل نظم { وربك فكبر } ( المدثر : 3 ) أي لا تترك تطهير ثيابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثياب can mean garments literally or metonymically the person wearing them; ʿAntarah’s line فشككت بالرمح الأصم ثيابه uses it for the person pierced.
rows.anchor: وللثياب إطلاق صريح وهو ما يلبسه اللابس ، وإطلاق كنائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification can mean literal cleaning and removing impurity or figurative moral purification, as in 33:33; both senses apply here, yielding physical and moral purification.
rows.anchor: وللتطهير إطلاق حقيقي وهو التنظيف وإزالة النجاسات وإطلاق مجازي وهو التزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands both actual cleanliness of clothing, correcting the pre-Islamic lack of concern for it, and moral purification of the self.
rows.anchor: فتحمل عليهما معا فتحصل أربعة معان لأنه مأمور بالطهارة الحقيقية لثيابه إبطالا لما كان عليه أهل الجاهلية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Among reports supporting the cleanliness sense, the strongest cited is the Tirmidhi hadith God is clean and loves cleanliness; al-Tirmidhi calls it gharīb.
rows.anchor: وأقواها ما رواه الترمذي ( إن الله نظيف يحب النظافة ) . وقال : هو غريب
